Start Before the first record

What it is · See how one coffee's records link up

Every record sits somewhere on this path. You use only the part you need: a home brewer may only ever touch the last two, a grower who sells cherry only the first two.

  1. Plot
  2. Harvest
  3. Process run
  4. Green lot
  5. Roast
  6. Cup

Each arrow is a link the app keeps for you. A green lot made from a run knows its run; the run knows its harvests; the harvests know their plots. Nothing is typed twice.

Harvest The day's picking

Step 4 · Weigh the baskets

Under Weights, tap + Add basket once for each basket, picker or batch. Put a name in the left box and the kilos in the box marked kg. The total adds up as you type: 3 · total 56 kg beside the button and Total cherry 56 kg from 3 baskets below.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromLogging a harvest, step 4

Watch out

A weight in the name box. If the kilos go into the left box, the app reads them as a name: the total does not grow and no Total cherry line appears. Look for the total after every row; if it is missing, move the number into the kg box.

Seen fromLogging a harvestRecords you can trust

Tip

One row called Day total with the day's kilos works as well. Separate rows show who picked what, or help to pay by weight.

Seen fromLogging a harvest

Process run Cherry to green

What it is

A run follows one batch through floating, pulping, fermentation, washing, drying, resting and hulling. It takes its cherry from your harvests, so it already knows the plots, and the green lot made at the end takes its weight from the run.

Seen fromProcess runsOne coffee, one chain

Step 3 · Take the cherry from my harvests

Under Source harvests, tick the harvests in this batch; each shows its code, date and kilos. Cherry in adds up. For cherry not logged as a harvest, leave them unticked and type the kilos in Cherry in (if not from harvests). Check Started.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 3One coffee, one chain

Step 5

To build your own list, choose a step type in the box under the steps and tap + Add step. The new step starts its clock straight away, with In kg taken from the last step's Out kg. ↑ moves a step up; × removes it.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 5

Step 7 · Weigh what goes in and out

Type In kg and Out kg, and the step's other boxes: floaters, water, the vessel or bed, notes.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromProcess runs, step 7

Watch out

Out more than in. If a step's Out kg is bigger than its In kg, the app says what to check. It does the same if the first step takes more than its harvests weighed. An example: Pulping: out 90 kg is more than in 85 kg. It never changes your numbers. Usually a number went into the wrong box.

Seen fromProcess runsRecords you can trust

Why it matters

Cup quality is often made or lost in processing. With each run's times, kilos and readings kept, this season's best lot can be set beside last season's. Outturn (green out as a share of cherry in) is worked out once the green weight is known.

Seen fromProcess runsQuality as you go

Green lot What goes to the roaster

What it is

A green lot is what goes to the roaster. Your own coffee points back to its run, and through it to the harvests and plots. Bought coffee keeps its origin as the seller states it. Every roast later picks a green lot as its source, and the stock goes down by itself.

Seen fromGreen lotsOne coffee, one chain

Step 2

Under From process, pick the run. Its chain shows, and a message: Green weight filled from the run, with the kilos from the run's last Out kg. Change it if the scale says otherwise.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 2One coffee, one chain

Step 3 · Record the weight and what it cost

Under This lot, check the Green weight (required). Type the Cost of this lot: what you paid, or what it cost to grow and process. The cost per green kilo shows, and about what a roasted kilo costs at 15% weight loss. Add Bags and Bag size if it is bagged.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 3

Step 5 · Add water to reach a target moisture

Open Rehydration (from All features). Type Moisture now, %, Target moisture, % and Batch you want at the end, kg. It shows Weigh out green coffee and Add water. Water in kg is the same as litres. Add it slowly while mixing, then let the coffee rest sealed so it soaks in evenly.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 5Quality as you go

Watch out

A green weight above what the run gave out saves too, with Green weight … kg is more than the process gave out. Your number is kept. Check the scale, or the run's last step.

Seen fromGreen lotsRecords you can trust

Step 8 · See how much is left

Tap Quality and stock: the kilos left, how many full bags that makes, and where it is stored. Roasts take their kilos off by themselves.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 8

Step 9 · Record a sample, sale, count or new moisture

For anything else, add a line. + Moisture is a new moisture reading (every reading is kept, so you can watch it in storage). + Count/move is for after counting or moving bags. + Adjust is for anything else. Fill it in, tap Add line, then Save at the bottom.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 9Quality as you go

Passport What a buyer can check

Step 7 · Split a lot into retail packs

Under Packs, Split into packs: how many, grams each, and whether they come from roasts or stock held. Each pack gets its own QR, and pack weights are checked against what was roasted or held.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 7One coffee, one chain

Step 8 · Send a lot to a buyer

Under Hand over, type the Buyer email, a name to show if you like, and the Weight sent, kg, then tap Sign and send. The buyer confirms on their own phone the weight they received, and can add their own roasts to the same passport. Their email is only used to reach them, never shown.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 8One coffee, one chain

What it is

The passport adds up the weights along the chain. Weights add up means nobody sent or roasted more than they held.

Seen fromPassports and selling into EuropeRecords you can trust

Step 9 · Receive a lot someone sent me

When a farm hands over a lot, you get an email. Sign in and open Passports. Under Lots sent to you, the lot waits with the weight the farm says it sent. Weigh the coffee, type the Weight you received, kg and tap Confirm receipt. This is signed with your phone and adds the lot to your green coffee in Origin. See passport opens the lot's page first.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 9One coffee, one chain

Roast Heat and time

What it is

A roast that names its green lot carries the lot's chain with it: plot, harvest, run and lot. The lot's stock goes down by the green weight you roast, and the roast shows on the lot and on its passport.

Seen fromRoastingOne coffee, one chain

Step 3 · Say which coffee I am roasting

In the timer, under Roaster and coffee identity, pick the Source green lot. The estate, coffee code and moisture fill in from the lot. Add the Roast number, the Green weight g, the Charge temperature °C and your Machine / roaster profile if you like.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 3One coffee, one chain

Step 8 · Finish and keep the roast

Tap Finish. Under Result, type the Roasted weight g and the Final roast colour: total time, development, development % and weight loss work themselves out. Tap Save on device.

Seen fromRoasting, step 8Quality as you go

Cup Brew, cup and taste

Tip

A Bluetooth scale can fill the coffee and water weights. Open the page in Chrome on Android, or in the Bluefy browser on iPhone; the form says so.

Business People, work, sales, land

Step 3 · Work out the month's wages

Month and wages adds up days, overtime, piece work from Field jobs, advances and the net pay, ready to print. Leave and holidays keeps leave, holidays and bonuses.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRunning the business, step 3

Step 4 · Record work done by the piece

Open Jobs and tap ＋ New job: the date, the kind of work (picking, weeding, pruning and more) and the place. Pay by quantity, days, hours or a fixed sum; the rate last used for that work fills in. Put each worker's quantity and save. Mark the job done to send it to the month's wages.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRunning the business, step 4

Step 5 · Record a sale

Open Sales and money and tap ＋ Sale. Pick the buyer and product from your lists, the quantity and the rate; the amount works itself out. A green lot can fill it. The buyer's GSTIN and credit days show, and the payment due date fills in. Dispatch, inside the sale, keeps the transporter, vehicle, e-way bill, freight and dates.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRunning the business, step 5One coffee, one chain

Step 7 · See who owes what

Receipts is money in from buyers; Payments is money out (a supplier with a UPI ID gets a Pay by UPI link). Summary shows payments due and late, totals for each month, and what each buyer owes. Export to CSV for your accountant.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRunning the business, step 7

Help Snags and words

What it is

A number in the wrong box. Weights that do not add up are flagged when you save. Examples: a basket total that never appears, a step whose Out kg is more than its In kg, a green weight above what the run gave. The app never changes your numbers; it tells you what to check. Open the record, move the number, save. The change is kept beside the record.

Seen fromWhen something goes wrong, and the words usedRecords you can trust
